title: It 2
subtitle: I hate it that ... / There's no denying that ...
summary: Use it as the object of a verb pointing forward to a clause, and choose between It is no ... and There is no ... .

lesson.heading: it as the object of a verb
lesson.text: Some verbs need **it** before a clause. **can't bear, hate, like, love, resent** and **can't stand** take it before a that-, if- or when-clause; **dislike, enjoy, prefer** and **understand** take it before an if- or when-clause.

examples.text: I hate **it** that you can swim so well and I can't.
examples.wrong: I hate that you can swim so well

examples.text: We always enjoy **it** when they stay with us.
examples.wrong: We always enjoy when they stay with us

lesson.heading: Optional it, or no it at all

left.label: it is optional, especially in speech
examples: You've just got to accept **(it)** that Emil's gone and won't be coming back.

right.label: never with it
examples: I can't remember when I last saw her. (not ... remember **it** when ...)
Also: argue, discover, emphasise, notice, predict.

lesson.heading: it + adjective / noun phrase + clause
lesson.text: With verbs that say how we see a situation - **believe, consider, feel, find** (= discover from experience), **think** - it comes first, then an adjective or noun phrase, then the clause. With **leave** and **owe** we can add *to somebody* + a to-infinitive.

examples.text: Officials said they believe **it unlikely that** any lasting damage to the environment has been done.
examples.note: or ... they believe it is unlikely that ...; not they believe unlikely that ...

examples.text: Don't bother to arrange anything. Just leave **it to me to sort out**.
She owed **it to** her parents **to do** well at college.

lesson.heading: it + as + noun / adjective + clause
lesson.text: With **accept, regard, see, take** (= interpret in a particular way) and **view** we use it + *as*.

examples.text: We see **it as** an insult to have received no reply to our letter.
I take **it as** encouraging when students attend all my lectures.

lesson.heading: It is no ... and There is no ...
rows: It's no secret that he wants a new job.
There's no denying that he's intelligent.
It's no surprise that his latest film has been so successful.
There's no alternative (or choice) but to ask her to leave.
It's no use telling me now. I needed to know a week ago.
There's no hope of getting more money.
It's no good getting angry. That won't help solve the problem.
There's no need to explain how it works; I'll read the manual.
It's no coincidence (or accident) that they left the party at the same time.
There's no point in buying an ice-cream maker unless you plan to use it a lot.
It's no longer necessary to have a visa to visit the country.
There's no question of agreeing to his demands. / There's no reason to be pessimistic.

lesson.heading: Only the It is no ... sentences can be turned round
lesson.text: With **It is / was no ...** we can move the that-, -ing or to-infinitive clause to the front. With **There is / was no ...** we cannot.

examples.text: It's no secret that he wants a new job.
examples.note: or That he wants a new job is no secret.

examples.text: There's no denying that he's intelligent.
examples.wrong: That he's intelligent is no denying

lesson.text: If you can rewrite the sentence starting with the that-clause, it is an It is no ... expression; if you cannot, it is a There is no ... one.

exercises.prompt: She ___ when people criticise her work, and she gets very upset.
exercises.explanation: can't bear needs it before a when-clause.

exercises.statement: We always enjoy it when they stay with us.
exercises.explanation: Correct. enjoy needs it before a when-clause.

exercises.prompt: I ___ hard to understand why the film was made in black and white and not colour.

exercises.statement: I hate that you can swim so well and I can't.
exercises.explanation: I hate it that you can swim so well and I can't. hate needs it before a that-clause.

exercises.prompt: Match the halves of these fixed expressions.

pairs.right: telling me now. I needed to know a week ago.
buying an ice-cream maker unless you plan to use it a lot.
explain how it works; I'll read the manual.
they left the party at the same time.
his latest film has been so successful.

exercises.prompt: ___ that Julia and Jakub have split up. Everyone in the office knows.
exercises.explanation: It's no secret that ... - and we could also say That Julia and Jakub have split up is no secret.

exercises.prompt: My contact lens must have fallen out in the snow, so ___ of finding it.
Officials said they believe ___ that any lasting damage to the environment has been done.
exercises.explanation: believe takes it + adjective + that-clause (or ... believe it is unlikely that ...).

exercises.prompt: We ___ to our supporters to play to the best of our ability in the match.
exercises.explanation: owe it to somebody to do something = have a responsibility to them.

exercises.statement: That he's intelligent is no denying.
exercises.explanation: There's no denying that he's intelligent. There is no ... expressions cannot be turned round.

exercises.prompt: ___ possible to buy tickets at the theatre. You have to buy them online.
exercises.explanation: It's no longer + adjective = it used to be so, but is not now.

exercises.prompt: A new managing director opens his first speech to the board. Put his words in order.
exercises.answer: I take it as a great honour to be asked to become managing director of Rexco.
exercises.explanation: take, see, accept, regard and view use it + as + noun phrase + clause.
